name: Giovanni Trapattoni
scopeNote: Style is 'gioco all'italiana' / zona mista (TFT: a combination of man-marking and zonal marking), an evolution of Rocco's catenaccio, not pure catenaccio and not pure zonal. Spell dates are month-level (first/last day of the month assumed; TFT: took over Juventus July 1976; Bayern 1994-95 and 1996-98 per bundesliga.com). Counted: Juventus I, Inter, Juventus II, Bayern II. Digest is mostly retrospective (TFT 2016-2020); no contemporary dated sources found, so all facts retrospectiveOnly. Marking evolution over the career (Juve man-marker Gentile plus roaming libero, later Inter with Mandorlini/Ferri) is thinly sourced.
openQuestions: Exact day dates of each spell not confirmed against a second source.
How marking changed from Juventus 1976-86 to Inter 1986-91 and Bayern: only Inter back-line composition found; no primary contemporary source.
No verified source on pressing: the pressing/defensive block was low-to-mid block with counter-attacks per TFT, but 'pressing' not described.
Italian Wikiquote Trapattoni quote on difesa mista has no date or source.
TFT says the 1982 Platini/Boniek era brought a more attacking phase, while Il Foglio stresses defensivism: label disagreement.
